content: Pseudodiarrhea, previously referred to as hyperdefecation, is characterized by an increased frequency of bowel movements, defined as more than three stools per day, while maintaining a normal stool weight of less than 300 grams per day (Fine and Schiller, 1999). This condition is frequently associated with rectal urgency and is commonly observed in patients with irritable bowel syndrome, hyperthyroidism, or anorectal disorders such as proctitis. In some cases, individuals with rectal obstruction, such as those caused by fecal impaction or the presence of a vaginal pessary, may also exhibit symptoms of pseudodiarrhea. This occurs because only liquid stool is able to bypass the obstruction (Chou and Yu, 2003; Tatar and Trivedi, 2005). It is important to note that pseudodiarrhea may be more prevalent than chronic diarrhea. Therefore, it should always be considered as a potential diagnosis in patients presenting with complaints of chronic diarrhea.
